sentences.text: This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by the petitioners under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the Act') challenging the judgment and award dated 05.08.2017 passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge & MACT-VII, Vijayapura, (for short hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1483/2014 seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
Appellants are the petitioners and the respondents are the respondents before the Tribunal.
3. Facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that, on 15.07.2014 at 4.00 p.m., the deceased Lalemashak @ Ladlemashak S/o: Bashasab Walikar, serving as Field Officer in PACL Company.
On the same day, he was proceeding towards Goa along with his colleagues to attend the company meeting in a Car bearing registration No.KA-28/N-0795 belonging to one of his colleagues.

While proceeding on Belagavi-Khanapur road near NC: 2024:KHC-K:3829-DB Hattaragungi cross on 2 km away from Khanapur, the driver of the said Car drove it in a speed in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over it and made it turn topple down by the side of the road, resulting in the accident.
Due to the said impact, inmates of the Car sustained severe injuries.
Ladlemashak also sustained grievous injuries on his body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Hospital at Belagavi.
Due to the injuries, he succumbed to the injuries.
A criminal case was registered against the driver of the Car.
It is contended that the deceased was hale and healthy aged about 30 years and drawing salary of Rs.3,32,065/- per annum and contributing the entire salary to the family welfare.
It is contended that the deceased was serving the registered firm and due to the loss of deceased, the petitioners are facing much inconvenience and difficulties.

The petitioners being the legal representatives of the deceased-Lalemashak @ Ladlemashak filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of Lalemashak @ Ladlemashak in the road traffic accident.
In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal and hence, he was placed exparte.

5. Respondent No.2/Insurance company filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation as claimed in the claim petition.
6. The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings of the parties, framed the issues.
In order to prove the case, the petitioners examined petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 got marked 13 documents as Exs.P1 to P13.
Respondent No.2 did not adduce any evidence but got marked the copy of insurance certificate marked as Ex.R1.

sentences.text: The Tribunal after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence answered issue No.1 in the affirmative, issue No.2 partly affirmative and issue No.3 as per final order.
The claim petition was allowed in part with costs.

It is ordered that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,33,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of entire amount and further held that respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed the respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount within a period of 30 days from the date of passing of the judgment.
8. The petitioners aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal have filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3829-DB 10.

The learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners submits that the petitioners have produced the income tax returns in order to establish the monthly income of the deceased and also examined PW.3- who is the Income Tax Officer.
The Tribunal has not considered the evidence of PW.3 and income tax assessments returns at Exs.P11 to P13 and awarded compensation which is on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds he prays to allow the appeal.

11. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance company supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for interference and prays to dismiss the appeal.
12. Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The point that arises for consideration is with regard to quantum of compensation.

13. The petitioners in order to establish that the deceased Lalemashak @ Ladlemashak died in the road traffic accident have produced Ex.P1, the certified copy of FIR and Ex.P8, the certified copy of charge sheet.
Ex . P8
discloses that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. Insofar as quantum of compensation, it is the case of the petitioners that the deceased Lalemashak @ Ladlemashak was working as a Field Officer in PACL Company and getting salary of Rs.3,32,065/- per annum.

In order to prove that the deceased was working as a Field Officer in PACL Company, the petitioners have produced income tax assessment marked as Exs.P11 to 13,
which discloses that the deceased was getting an income of Rs.3,32,065/- per annum and there were Smt. Mehaboobi And Ors vs Sri. Lalsab And Anr on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60471550/
4 certain deductions to an extent of Rs.42,085/-.

sentences.text: Thus, the income of the deceased is comes to Rs.2,89,980/- per annum and NC: 2024:KHC-K:3829-DB after deduction of Rs.9,268/- towards income tax, it comes to Rs.2,80,712/- per annum.

Further, in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the income of the deceased has to be added towards the future prospects, which comes to Rs.3,92,996/-.

sentences.text: Since the petitioners are six in numbers, the appropriate deduction would be 1/4th towards the personal expenses of the deceased.
Thus, we assess the income of the deceased at Rs.2,94,747/- per annum (3,92,996 - 98,249).

The deceased was aged about 30 years as on the date of the accident,
the multiplier of 17 has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of 50,10,699/- under the head loss of future income.

15. Further, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3829-DB Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, each petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.

entities.text: Magma General - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3829-DB Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners are six in number, hence the compensation towards loss of consortium would be Rs.2,40,000/- (40,000 x 6).
In addition, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body.

16. Thus, in all, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.52,80,699/- as against Rs.10,33,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.42,47,699/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization of amount.

17. In view of the above discussion, We proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
iii. The petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.52,80,699/- as against Rs.10,33,000/-,.
iv. The petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.42,47,699/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization of amount.
